question.text: A soap bubble of the radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is formed inside another soap bubble of radius, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The radius of an equivalent soap bubble that has the same excess pressure as inside the smaller bubble with respect to the atmospheric pressure is____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text:
The formula of excess pressure inside the soap bubble is, 4TR here T is the surface tension and R is the radius of the soap bubble, 

⇒P0+4T6+4T3=P0+4TR

⇒16+13=1R⇒R=2 cm.
